C-REVIEW-PAIR-FIXTURES-1-429BFA80.Problem:
Four dedicated attempt-pair regression tests read the repository's published archive as their input: they name concrete publisher bundles, enumerate the `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-*` population, embed a frozen authoring-time membership list, and drive the real CLI against one publisher bundle's recorded ledger. The measured inputs:
- `src/review/core.test.ts:2175` — `live archive pairs that raised under the old rule are silent under both codes` runs `runReview` over the repository root for the named bundles `C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY` and `C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY`. - `src/review/core.test.ts:2198` — `historical close corpus: zero live and retired findings on the frozen 27` embeds `HISTORICAL_CLOSE_C_IDS` (built from `AUTHORING_ARCHIVE_C_IDS`, `src/review/core.test.ts:1981-2010`) and asserts those 27 directory names are present in the live archive before asserting zero live and retired findings over them. - `src/review/core.test.ts:2228` — `complete archive retired code: zero retired findings over every current C-*` enumerates every real `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-*` directory and asserts zero retired-code findings. - `src/review/core.test.ts:2250` — `T-005 warning remains observable through the real CLI` spawns the CLI against the publisher archived bundle `C-DECLARATION-GUARD-RETIRE-1-C69B6AB6` and reads its recorded ledger.
**Why this is a defect slice, not a nicety.** Those inputs make the regressions depend on publisher bundle names, on the historical population and its denominator, and on archived artifact formats. A bundle renamed, removed, or reshaped by unrelated publisher work silently changes or removes the input the test stands on; a denominator that only shrinks cannot answer the "did the audit actually look?" question the membership assertion existed to answer. The tests are current-behavior regressions and should not be anchored to the archive as a corpus.
**Obligations being replaced (passive rationale, not current validation).** `C-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-BASELINE-2-D5F2E1C3/spec.xml` carries `AC-HISTORICAL-MEMBERSHIP`, `AC-HISTORICAL-ZERO`, `AC-CURRENT-ARCHIVE-RETIRED-ZERO`, `AC-DETECTOR-PRESERVED`, and `AC-T005-OBSERVABLE`. `C-HISTORICAL-ASSERTION-REVIEW-2-67E62A9B/spec.xml` carries `AC-T005-GUARD`, `AC-PRESERVED-AUDITS`, and the selected-close obligations around them. `C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY/spec.xml` carries `AC-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-ZERO` and its `AC-T005-OBSERVABLE`. Those obligations are historical evidence for what the regressions were protecting; this bundle does not validate their archives, does not re-execute their commands, and does not treat their bytes as current input.
**Counterweights preserved.** The denominator-shrink counterweight is answered by explicit fixture presence and nonzero audited pair counts over the synthetic inputs: the audit must report it ran over at least one fail/pass pair, so a pass cannot come from an empty population. The detector-suppression counterweight is answered by the positive real-CLI warning: equal non-artifact source digests on a synthetic archived bundle must still raise the live finding through the CLI, so a silent detector cannot pass as a clean corpus.
**Scope discipline.** This is one dependency slice of publisher-input isolation, not a claim that the whole program is finished. Runtime implementation, other process-audit tests, status/context/calibration inputs, global consumer archive policy, XML-comment exceptions, and portable teaching remain outside this slice. `README.md` and `examples/` do not change because this slice changes internal test inputs only.
